title: Redox-Responsive 2-Aminoanthraquinone Core–Shell Particles for Structural Colors and Carbon Capture

compounds.name: 2-aminoanthraquinone
compounds.quote: The use of glycidyl methacrylate within the shell material oﬀers the possibility of a ring-opening reaction with the redox-responsive 2-aminoanthraquinone (2-AAQ), which possesses a high aﬃnity toward electrophilic carbon dioxide.

conditions.quote: For this purpose, the 2-AAQ-containing particles were analyzed by using CV using 1 M degassed sulfuric acid as an electrolyte as it provides the protons needed to address the immobilized 2-AAQ moieties in a potential range of −0.3 V to +0.3 V versus Ag/AgCl at a scan rate of 50 mV s−1.

conditions.electrolyte_text: 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium bis(triﬂuoromethylsulfonyl)imide (BMIM TFSI) room-temperature ionic liquid (RTIL) electrolyte
conditions.quote: This consisted of the 2-AAQ electrode, a porous separator, a counter electrode comprising a poly-vinylferrocene (PVFc)-CNT composite coated on carbon felt, and 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium bis(triﬂuoromethylsulfonyl)imide (BMIM TFSI) room-temperature ionic liquid (RTIL) electrolyte.

observations.quote: In aprotic electrolytes, the two-electron reduction of 2-AAQ generates two nucleophilic centers (Figure 4, ﬁrst reaction), which react with electrophilic CO2 to form the corresponding biscarbonate (below).
